title: A study on the relationship between adolescent new immigrants' adjustment in school and self-esteem
population: Adolescent new immigrants attending Hong Kong secondary schools
study_design: Quantitative questionnaire study
main_finding: Higher self-esteem was significantly associated with better peer relations, higher class rank, less difficulty with subject content and greater readiness to ask questions. 78.3% reported medium-to-high self-esteem, 82.6% medium-to-good peer relations, and nearly 40% ranked 1-10 in class. About 40% had not used adjustment programmes or school social work; awareness of these services was incomplete.
limitation: Cross-sectional associations cannot establish direction; single thesis sample; sampling and migration timing are not reported in the abstract; full text is restricted; mid-entry and prior schooling duration are not separable.

title: Grade level and achievement of immigrants' children: academic redshirting in Hong Kong
population: Fifteen-year-old Hong Kong PISA participants, including Mainland immigrant students; qualitative school visits supplement the analysis
study_design: Hong Kong PISA 2003 statistical analysis plus visits to three secondary schools and six focus groups with Mainland immigrant students in Grades 7-9
main_finding: Fifty-eight percent of Mainland immigrant students were below the modal grade. Same-age comparisons showed lower mathematics, reading and science scores, but controlling for grade reversed the estimated gap; Mainland immigrant repeaters also compared favorably with native repeaters. The article argues that school-system misalignment and lower grade placement must be considered when interpreting achievement gaps.
limitation: Observational PISA analysis cannot prove that lower placement caused better performance; immigrant subgroup analytic n is not clearly extractable from the accessible text; placement may reflect several mechanisms; 2003 data predate later reforms and cohorts.

title: Improving migrant children's self-esteem through a language enhancement programme
population: Migrant students in one Hong Kong secondary school and two tutors
study_design: Qualitative naturalistic case study of an English Enhancement Programme; repeated interviews, diaries/journals and external ratings
main_finding: The thesis reports that most participants showed noticeable gains in self-esteem and confidence speaking English under favorable circumstances, but individual responses varied. Outings, tutor encouragement, peer support and games were identified as helpful elements.
limitation: One school, 13 students, no control group and an intervention designed/researched in one context; changes cannot be causally attributed to the programme; detailed full text was not inspected; sample transfer histories are not reported in the abstract.

title: Resources mitigating the impediment of discrimination to the acculturation success of students migrated to Hong Kong
population: Students who migrated from Mainland China to Hong Kong since 1991 in 31 randomly sampled secondary schools
study_design: Cross-sectional school survey with regression/moderation analyses
main_finding: Earlier social integration tended to buffer the adverse association of discrimination with acculturation outcomes. Welfare receipt, affiliation with a Mainland home-place organization and Cantonese fluency showed some aggravating moderation patterns; Cantonese fluency also had generally beneficial main associations. The authors frame achievement and social integration as outcomes.
limitation: Cross-sectional and partly retrospective self-report; moderation is not causal; constructs embed a structural-functionalist and normatively host-integration framing; the counterintuitive Cantonese interaction should not be simplified; school and family heterogeneity are incompletely visible in the abstract.

author_year: Luk-Fong, Yuk Yee Pattie; Brennan, Marie (2010)
title: Teachers' experience of secondary education reform in Hong Kong
population: Secondary-school teachers implementing Hong Kong reforms
study_design: Life-narrative qualitative study
main_finding: Teachers described glocal mixtures: pupil-centredness, learning-to-learn, life-wide learning, assessment for learning and school-based assessment coexisted with teacher-centred pedagogy, emphasis on academic achievement and high-stakes examinations. They perceived both tensions and opportunities.
limitation: Teacher narratives, not newcomer student experiences; 24-person qualitative sample; 2010 reform stage; cultural labels in the article should not be treated as homogeneous system traits.

title: Assessment trends in Hong Kong: Seeking to establish formative assessment in an examination culture
population: Hong Kong school assessment policy and practice literature
study_design: Policy and literature analysis
main_finding: Hong Kong policy has promoted assessment for learning since the 1990s, but the paper finds limited change in school assessment practice. It describes persistence of competitive paper-and-pencil assessment and warns that school-based assessment can become more frequent summative testing rather than formative practice.
limitation: Not an original newcomer study and not a systematic review; broad historical-cultural framing risks essentializing examination culture; evidence predates current reforms and cohorts.

author_year: Zhu, Yan; Leung, Frederick K. S. (2011)
title: Mathematics achievement of Mainland immigrant students in Hong Kong
population: Hong Kong Grade 8 TIMSS participants classified by immigrant status
study_design: Secondary analysis comparing four TIMSS rounds
main_finding: Across the four rounds, the relative mathematics performance of students classified as first-generation immigrants showed marked deterioration compared with native students; the paper explores possible internal and external explanations.
limitation: TIMSS did not directly report actual birthplace; authors used non-local birth and census evidence as a proxy for Mainland origin. Exact subgroup n and detailed covariates were unavailable from the abstract; repeated cross-sections do not track individual adaptation or identify causes.

title: Linking motivation and pedagogy: The case of newly-arrived Hong Kong students
population: Students who moved from Mainland China to Hong Kong for family reunion during the prior ten years
study_design: Quantitative questionnaire adapted from Dörnyei's motivational framework
main_finding: Social integration and desire for success were the most influential reported motivational subcomponents for English learning in this sample.
limitation: Sample size, grades, school types and arrival timing were not reported in the accessible article abstract; cross-sectional motivation measures are not attainment or causal effects; no DOI was found in official metadata.

author_year: Gu, Ming Yue Michelle; Qu, Xiaoyuan Doris (2015)
title: Ideological disqualification in language use: Being newcomers in primary education
population: Immigrant Mainland Chinese pupils and teachers in one Hong Kong primary school with a large immigrant intake
study_design: Qualitative interview study
main_finding: The study identifies institutional disqualification of parts of pupils' emergent repertoires and students' internalization of teacher language attitudes, including censoring native-language use. It argues that flexible multilingual ideologies can reposition students' resources as symbolic assets.
limitation: One-school qualitative study; sample size, pupil grades and migration histories were not available in the abstract; the article analyzes language ideology rather than measured academic outcomes.

author_year: Wu, Qiaobing; Ou, Ying; Jordan, Lucy P. (2020)
title: Mapping the cultural identities of youths in Hong Kong from a social capital perspective
population: Local, cross-border and new immigrant students; NIS were born in Mainland China and had lived in Hong Kong less than seven years
study_design: School-based multistage cluster survey and logistic regression
main_finding: Among NIS, 60.4% reported dual Hong Kong-and-Chinese identity. Better peer relationships were associated with lower odds of confused identity; parent-child interaction was positively associated with dual identity, while parental monitoring showed different associations with Chinese and dual identification.
limitation: Cross-sectional data cannot establish effects; cultural identity is a single-choice item; only three high-concentration districts were sampled; no transfer timing or prior schooling; same 2016-2017 Hong Kong dataset underlies D1-018 and related 2021 work, so these are not independent samples.

author_year: Jiang, Hechao; Shek, Daniel T. L.; Law, Moon Y. M. (2021)
title: Differences between Chinese Adolescent Immigrants and Adolescent Non-Immigrants in Hong Kong: Perceived Psychosocial Attributes, School Environment and Characteristics of Hong Kong Adolescents
population: Mainland Chinese adolescent immigrants and Hong Kong non-immigrant adolescents in 20 local secondary schools
study_design: Stratified cluster cross-sectional questionnaire and ANCOVA with demographic controls
main_finding: Groups did not differ on most outcomes. Immigrant adolescents reported higher moral character, empathy and social trust, and more favorable perceived school environments, including teacher-student relations and teachers' social-emotional/positive-behavior techniques.
limitation: Cross-sectional self-report and perception measures; immigrant status does not specify duration, transfer point or prior schooling; age distributions differ; results cannot establish that migration or pedagogical style caused differences.

author_year: Dou, Diya; Shek, Daniel T. L. (2022)
title: Hong Kong high school students' perceptions of the new secondary school curriculum
population: Hong Kong Secondary 6 students in 28 schools; immigrant subgroup not reported
study_design: Self-report questionnaire; CFA, paired t tests and MANOVA using the final wave of a six-year project
main_finding: Most students liked the curriculum and perceived noncognitive benefits, but substantial minorities were negative, especially about senior secondary education. Junior-secondary perceptions were more positive; high-performing students reported the most favorable perceptions and low-performing students the least.
limitation: Not an immigrant study; one final-wave self-report analysis cannot establish curriculum effects; achievement is self-rated; abstract says data in 2015 whereas methods describe the 2015/2016 final wave; no newcomer subgroup.

title: Understanding the Impact of Cross-Border Migration on Children's Well-Being in Mainland China and Hong Kong
population: NIS, cross-border, Hong Kong local and Hong Kong-born Mainland-schooled students; NIS born in Mainland and resident in Hong Kong less than seven years
study_design: 2016-2017 cross-sectional school survey; propensity-score matching on observed characteristics
sample_size: 2610 total: 348 NIS, 445 cross-border, 1387 Hong Kong local, 430 Hong Kong-born Mainland-schooled
main_finding: After matching, NIS exceeded matched local students on educational aspirations, last-term exam results, self-rated performance and importance of study, and reported lower study pressure; they also scored favorably on several mental-health, resilience and relationship indicators. Compared with cross-border students, NIS had more grade repetition and lower life satisfaction but similar other educational outcomes.
limitation: All outcomes self-reported; PSM addresses observed rather than unobserved selection; cross-sectional data do not establish causal migration effects; three Hong Kong districts, pre-COVID data, school segregation and composition change limit generalization; same Hong Kong sample as D1-015 and related 2021 output.

author_year: Education Bureau, Government of the Hong Kong SAR
title: Initiation Programme for Newly Arrived Children
population: Newly arrived children from Mainland China and other eligible newcomer/returnee groups
study_design: Policy/programme description
main_finding: The voluntary full-time six-month Initiation Programme, operating since 2000, combines English, Chinese, learning skills, personal/social development, arts and physical education before mainstream placement. A separate 60-hour Induction Programme is available to eligible children who enter mainstream school directly.
limitation: Authoritative for programme design, not for uptake, implementation quality or effectiveness; webpage is continuously updated and has no clear publication year; it combines heterogeneous newcomer categories.

title: The nature of social media use and ethnic minorities’ acculturation
population: Ethnic minority secondary-school students in Hong Kong
study_design: Qualitative individual interviews
main_finding: Different social media experiences afforded different acculturation possibilities, but could also reproduce or amplify social power relations and struggles. The authors describe social media use and acculturation as context-dependent and cyclically interacting rather than as a one-way platform effect.
limitation: Not mainland-to-Hong Kong migrants; qualitative self-report; migration timing and school-entry timing are not established in the accessible abstract; full sampling and coding detail was not accessible, so platform-specific claims were not extracted beyond verified material.

title: Student migration and polymedia: mainland Chinese students’ communication media use in Hong Kong
population: Mainland Chinese students at three public and one private Hong Kong university
study_design: Long semi-structured interviews, observation, and voluntarily supplied profiles or communication records
main_finding: Media communication with family and friends in mainland China was described as intensive, intimate and emotion-oriented, supporting familiarity and belonging. Communication with Hong Kong contacts was more limited, functional and study-oriented, sometimes yielding practical help but also exposing tension; the contrast illustrates relationally differentiated polymedia rather than simple platform replacement.
limitation: Qualitative and nonrepresentative sample; university rather than school-age population; accounts from communication partners were absent; data reflect an earlier platform ecology and cannot establish causal effects on integration.

title: Exploring social media practices and cross-cultural adaptation of mobile students in multilingual and multicultural higher education
population: Mainland Chinese undergraduates admitted to three Hong Kong universities
study_design: Semi-structured interviews and narrative inquiry
main_finding: The authors report that critically reflective social media practices helped participants expand online and offline habitus and accumulate forms of capital relevant to university adaptation. They emphasize that any positive role depended on how tools were used, not merely on the platform selected.
limitation: Small purposive qualitative university sample; no secondary-school entrants; self-reported narratives; accessible material does not permit claims about prevalence or causal impact.

title: Birds of a feather flock even closer together in the digital era: The role of China’s parallel digital realm in the lives of migrant students in Hong Kong
population: Current and former mainland Chinese students who pursued bachelor’s degrees in Hong Kong
study_design: Semi-structured interviews with purposive, quota and limited snowball sampling; retrospective cross-cohort comparison
main_finding: Participants described Chinese platforms and co-national networks as sources of informational, emotional and instrumental support. The authors interpret this self-sufficient digital ecology as reducing some participants’ perceived need for local ties; platform and information differences also appeared in accounts of limited shared topics with locals.
limitation: Nonrepresentative interview sample; current students and graduates across a 25-year arrival span; substantial retrospective recall; university population; structural non-assimilation is an interpretive claim and cannot be treated as a causal or universal result.

title: Establishing ties or strengthening friendships? Students’ use of online social networks in intercultural friendship development
population: Mainland and Hong Kong student groups
study_design: Mixed methods: questionnaire and follow-up semi-structured interviews
main_finding: Instant messaging and social networking sites mainly helped maintain and strengthen existing friendships rather than initiate new ones. Instant messaging supported presence awareness and offline ties, while social networking sites helped reveal common interests as well as values and cultural differences.
limitation: Accessible abstract does not report school stage, recruitment sites or detailed platform measures; self-report and cross-sectional design; migration timing and target transfer status are absent.

title: Between WeChat and WhatsApp: translocal belonging among mainland Chinese professional migrants in Hong Kong
population: Mainland Chinese professional migrants in Hong Kong
study_design: Three rounds of fieldwork and in-depth interviews
main_finding: Participants primarily used WeChat for contingent intimacy, mainland family obligations and some survival or resource needs in Hong Kong, while WhatsApp was used for local integration and professional communication. Cross-platform belonging was entangled with surveillance, multilingual pressure, exclusion concerns and life stage.
limitation: Educated professional adults rather than adolescents; small qualitative sample; platform functions may be occupation-specific; full text was not accessible and no prevalence or causal conclusion is warranted.

title: Multiliteracies on Instant Messaging in Negotiating Local, Translocal, and Transnational Affiliations: A Case of an Adolescent Immigrant
population: One adolescent girl who migrated from China to the United States
study_design: In-depth case study using screen recordings, interviews, observations, qualitative coding and orthographic analysis
main_finding: The participant used multilingual and multimodal instant messaging to sustain simultaneous affiliations with a local Chinese immigrant community, translocal Asian-American youth and peers in China, while developing a repertoire usable across communities.
limitation: Single case; United States rather than Hong Kong; older instant-messaging ecology; no group-level inference or causal claim is possible.

title: Digital Escapes? ICTs, Settlement and Belonging among Karen Youth in Melbourne, Australia
population: Karen youth from refugee backgrounds participating in the Home Lands digital-media project
study_design: Participatory digital-media project and qualitative analysis of three media products
main_finding: The analyzed films and other media products showed several ways of imagining home and navigating Karen, refugee, youth and Australian identifications. Digital production and circulation opened spaces for negotiating local and transnational belonging but remained embedded in material settlement conditions.
limitation: Overall participant count not reported in accessible material; three selected products; project facilitation shapes what was produced; refugee resettlement differs materially from mainland-to-Hong Kong school transfer.

author_year: Yuhui Olivia Chen; Cherrie Joy Billedo (2025)
title: Crossing digital borders: Exploring the role of non-Chinese social media use in the cross-cultural adaptation of Chinese international students
population: Mainland Chinese citizens studying outside mainland China
study_design: Preregistered cross-sectional survey and structural equation modeling
main_finding: Higher non-Chinese social media engagement was associated with higher psychological and sociocultural adaptation. The psychological association was stronger among respondents intending to remain in the host country. Engagement included time, behaviors, platform breadth, relationship use, self-disclosure and emotional attachment.
limitation: Cross-sectional convenience and snowball sample; self-report; predominantly postgraduate and university population; 25 host countries pooled; associations cannot show that platform engagement causes adaptation or that users abandoned Chinese platforms.

author_year: Joep Hofhuis; Marieke C. van Egmond; Franziska E. Lutz; Karin von Reventlow; Anette Rohmann (2023)
title: The effect of social network sites on international students’ acculturation, adaptation, and wellbeing
population: International students in the Netherlands and Chinese international students in Germany
study_design: Two cross-sectional questionnaire studies with mediation models
main_finding: Across the two samples, host-society SNS contact was positively related to adaptation. Home-culture SNS contact appeared negatively related to adaptation and indirectly to wellbeing in the authors’ models.
limitation: Two convenience and cross-sectional university samples; self-report; generic or Facebook-centered SNS measures; mediation does not establish temporal causality; contexts differ from Hong Kong adolescents.

title: Social media use and adaptation among Chinese students beginning to study in the United States
population: Mainland Chinese international university students in the United States for less than one year
study_design: Online cross-sectional questionnaire and path analysis
main_finding: More frequent pre-departure SNS use was associated with larger and more diverse networks abroad; network diversity was in turn associated with higher reported social and academic adaptation.
limitation: Purposive and respondent-driven university sample; cross-sectional retrospective self-report; United States context; no target-age participants or platform-specific transition; path analysis cannot establish causal sequence.

title: Digital Journeys: A Perspective on Understanding the Digital Experiences of International Students
population: International students
study_design: Conceptual synthesis
main_finding: The paper proposes a digital journey as movement from reliance on one bundle of digital information sources to a new, host-based or transnational bundle. The framework implies repertoire reconfiguration rather than automatic one-for-one platform replacement.
limitation: Conceptual rather than empirical; developed for international higher education; does not test mechanisms, outcomes or Hong Kong school-age experience.

author_year: Yik Wong Tseung; Binyu Xie; Ziting Peng (2024)
title: Virtual Parallel Societies—A Study on the Differences in Mobile Application Usage Between Hong Kong and Mainland Chinese Adolescents
population: Adolescents sampled separately in Hong Kong and mainland China; not migrants
study_design: Mixed methods using secondary QuestMobile and Hong Kong government data, semi-structured interviews and stated content analysis
sample_size: 12 interview participants from each region, plus secondary aggregate datasets
main_finding: The paper reports greater preference for global platforms such as Instagram and Facebook in its Hong Kong material and for WeChat and Weibo in its mainland material, and interprets the differences as informational silos.
limitation: No migrants or transfer students; recruitment, age composition and analytic integration are opaque; small regional interview samples are combined with aggregate data; strong deterministic and normative conclusions exceed the design; journal peer-review status was not confirmed.

title: Identity negotiation on the LIHKG platform: a grounded theory study of Mainland Chinese immigrants’ adaptation to Hong Kong society
population: Mainland Chinese immigrants using or discussing the LIHKG platform
study_design: Grounded-theory analysis combining platform posts and in-depth interviews
main_finding: The study identifies context-dependent integrative, confrontational, collaborative and avoidance patterns rather than fixed types. Political topics heightened boundaries, while professional and everyday topics more often enabled collaboration; online posts and interviews sometimes differed in political expression.
limitation: Participant ages and youth status are not established; LIHKG users and posts are self-selective and platform-specific; online authorship and demographic identity are difficult to verify; grounded-theory patterns are not prevalence estimates.

author_year: Rahmat Fadhli; Shanton Chang; Antonette Mendoza (2026)
title: Charting the initial digital journeys of students in a new digital environment: a qualitative study
population: Newly arrived international degree students at higher-education institutions in several Indonesian cities
study_design: Phenomenological qualitative study using one-to-one semi-structured interviews
main_finding: Participants moved iteratively through digital shock, transition and engagement or disengagement. Unfamiliar apps, language, usability and device capacity posed barriers; peer help, university guidance and digital skills supported adjustment. Outcomes included passive local information exposure, overload and improved local-language skills, and students often blended rather than replaced home and host tools.
limitation: University and Indonesia context; cross-sectional retrospective interviews rather than direct six-month tracking; heterogeneous national origins; student voices only; no causal estimate of effects on social integration.

title: El papel de las redes sociales digitales en la integración de los jóvenes migrantes marroquíes en España
population: Moroccan migrant youth who moved to Spain as minors; all interviewees male and recruited through an NGO-linked setting
study_design: In-depth interviews plus non-systematic participant observation
main_finding: Participants used WhatsApp prominently for family contact with Morocco and several platforms for peers and information. They described digital communication as supporting transnational family wellbeing and contact with new actors in Spain; examples also show that some Spanish friendships began offline at school, centers or through mutual contacts and were then maintained online.
limitation: Small all-male NGO-linked purposive sample; ages include young adults; Spain and unaccompanied-minor migration context differ from Hong Kong; self-report and non-systematic observation; peer-review policy was not confirmed; no causal inference.

title: Immigrant Children in Primary Schools in Hong Kong: Their Adjustment and the Role of Civic Education
population: Newly arrived mainland children and local classmates in three Hong Kong primary schools, with school staff and teacher-trainee informants
study_design: Three-school case study using pupil questionnaires, staff interviews, teacher-trainee interviews, and curriculum analysis
main_finding: The thesis reports generally positive overall adjustment alongside interaction difficulties. School staff linked some difficulties to cultural background and age gaps; schools with higher proportions of newly arrived pupils appeared to report fewer interaction problems, and the school was identified as a major source of help.
limitation: Doctoral thesis rather than peer-reviewed article; exact pupil N was not extracted; three-school design; staff attributions may reproduce assimilation assumptions; no causal test of school composition

author_year: Wong, Daniel Fu Keung; Lam, Debbie; Yan, Phyllis; Hung, Marion (2004)
title: The impacts of acculturative stress and social competence on the mental health of Mainland Chinese immigrant youth in Hong Kong
population: Mainland Chinese immigrant youth in Hong Kong
study_design: Cross-sectional structured questionnaire
main_finding: Survival issues and losses were rated as more stressful than cultural differences or unmet expectations. Self-control, empathy, assertiveness, and capacity to read social cues were associated with mental health and moderated some stress relationships.
limitation: Cross-sectional and self-report; school stage, migration duration, and mid-entry status are unclear; possible overlap with the immigrant subgroup in D3-015; moderation does not prove protection causally

author_year: Wong, Daniel F. K.; Yan, Phyllis; Lo, Eva; Hung, Marion (2003)
title: Mental health and social competence of Mainland Chinese immigrant and local youth in Hong Kong: A comparison
population: Mainland Chinese immigrant and local youth in Hong Kong
study_design: Cross-sectional structured questionnaire and group comparison
main_finding: Immigrant youth reported better mental health in this sample, whereas local youth scored higher on overall social competence. Within the immigrant group, stronger social competence was associated with better mental health.
limitation: Cross-sectional self-report; school stage and migration timing unclear; likely shares the 106-person immigrant sample with D3-014 and therefore is not independent confirmation

author_year: Lam, M. C.; Chan, T. S. (2004)
title: Life themes in the narratives of young Chinese immigrants who have successfully adjusted to life in Hong Kong
population: Young Chinese immigrants who moved to Hong Kong for family reunion and were selected as apparently well adjusted
study_design: Qualitative narrative interviews with purposively selected successful adjusters
main_finding: Narratives highlighted family, gratitude, face, learning, crisis, faith, and marginality; the authors also noted that developmental and socioeconomic contexts differentiated the groups.
limitation: Positive-case selection excludes poorly adjusted youth; accessible abstract does not report N or school entry timing; retrospective narrative themes cannot estimate population patterns

author_year: Shen, Yishan; Seo, Eunjin; Jiles, Alison I.; Zheng, Yao; Wang, Yijie (2022)
title: Language brokering and immigrant-origin youth's well-being: A meta-analytic review
population: Immigrant-origin youth who translate or mediate language for family members
study_design: Meta-analysis with moderator analyses
main_finding: Brokering frequency had small associations with weaker positive family relationships and socioemotional outcomes and slightly greater acculturative stress. Positive and negative feelings about brokering showed larger and directionally different associations, with effects varying by background and study characteristics.
limitation: Substantial heterogeneity; mainly family language brokering rather than school-peer cultural brokerage; settings differ from Hong Kong; mostly observational primary studies and no target-population estimate

title: Effects of cultural brokering on individual wellbeing and family dynamics among immigrant youth
population: First-generation Eastern European immigrant and refugee young adults
study_design: Cross-sectional survey with mediation analyses
main_finding: Negative feelings about language/cultural brokering were associated with depressive symptoms and family conflict; family conflict accounted for part of these associations. Role frequency and subjective appraisal were not interchangeable.
limitation: Young-adult, family-focused, US sample; cross-sectional mediation is not temporal causation; differs markedly from Hong Kong school-peer brokerage

title: When the Cultural Model of Success Fails: Mainland Chinese Teenage Immigrants in Hong Kong
population: Mainland Chinese teenagers who migrated to Hong Kong and entered mainstream secondary education
study_design: qualitative ethnographic/case-based analysis
main_finding: Migration- and school-related disadvantages can create a gap between expected and experienced educational success. The cases described students retaining the success model, individualising responsibility and guilt, and continuing to pursue it rather than rejecting it.
limitation: The accessible article does not tabulate a single analytic sample size; case-based findings are not prevalence estimates and concern an earlier migration-policy cohort.

author_year: Yuen, Celeste Y. M.; Wu, Rosalind (2011)
title: New Schooling and New Identities: Chinese Immigrant Students' Perspectives
population: Two Mainland-to-Hong Kong immigrant pupils plus one Shenzhen-resident cross-boundary pupil; only the two immigrant cases support target-population inferences
study_design: narrative interviews, school shadowing and follow-up
main_finding: The two migrant cases show concrete grade-placement and language transitions: one recently arrived pupil was placed two grades lower after a preparatory programme because of English; teacher and peer support, tutoring, mixed friendship circles and experiences of difference shaped academic and identity negotiation.
limitation: Only two target-population cases; one of the three cases is a daily cross-boundary student and is excluded from direct inference; schools and family resources differ, so no prevalence claims are possible.

author_year: Zhang, Shiyi; Wu, Qi; Chen, Xuhua (2025)
title: Cultural Distance and Social Needs: The Dynamic Adjustment Mechanisms of Social Support Among Newly Arrived Students in Hong Kong
population: Newly arrived students from Mainland China residing in Hong Kong for less than one year at one local secondary school
study_design: exploratory mixed methods: questionnaire, semi-structured interviews, descriptive statistics and thematic/grounded coding
main_finding: Students described complementary ties rather than one uniform integration path: Mainland ties were used mainly for emotional support, local Hong Kong ties for academic help and everyday companionship, and Hong Kong peers with Mainland backgrounds for both functions as relational bridges. Classroom grouping, clubs and online chat groups were interaction arenas.
limitation: Single immigrant-concentration school; small non-probability frame; 47 valid questionnaires are inadequate for strong psychometric or population claims; cross-sectional self-report; the paper does not document named platform portfolios.

title: Cross-cultural experiences of immigrant students from Mainland China in Hong Kong secondary schools
population: Mainland Chinese immigrant students in six Hong Kong secondary schools
study_design: unstructured interviews; two representative cases presented
main_finding: Students' narratives linked adaptation to language, cultural support and identity. They could acquire aspects of the new environment while maintaining Mainland identification, and some used meritocratic interpretations as agency in responding to discrimination and reduced cultural support.
limitation: Arrival grade, length of prior Mainland schooling and school placement are not reported in the accessible abstract; only two cases are presented in depth; findings predate recent migration cohorts.

title: 'I am not qualified to be a Honkongese because of my accented Cantonese': Mainland Chinese immigrant students in Hong Kong
population: A group of Mainland Chinese immigrant students at one Hong Kong secondary school
study_design: semi-structured interviews and school observations
main_finding: The school context positioned Putonghua marginally relative to Cantonese and English. Students responded by mobilising linguistic and cultural resources, sustaining Putonghua-speaking networks and imagining multilingual identities rather than simply abandoning their prior language.
limitation: The accessible abstract does not state sample size, arrival grade, years in Hong Kong or prior Mainland schooling; one-school design; language ideology cannot be reduced to individual proficiency.

author_year: Lee, Francis Wing-Lin; Chen, Timothy Ka-Kit (2005)
title: Service needs of young new arrivals from Mainland China to Hong Kong
population: Young new arrivals from Mainland China who had lived in Hong Kong for up to four years
study_design: in-depth qualitative interviews
main_finding: Participants described intertwined language, schooling, family, leisure and social-relationship needs. School-related accounts included fit and placement concerns and contrasts in discipline and homework, while informal and formal support networks varied.
limitation: Very small purposive social-service sample; not all participants were necessarily enrolled in the target grades; arrival and placement histories varied; service-need framing may overrepresent difficulties.

title: Assimilation, integration and the construction of identity: The experience of Chinese cross-boundary and newly arrived students in Hong Kong schools
population: Nine newly arrived Mainland-born students and nine cross-boundary students; the groups are analysed comparatively
study_design: in-depth student and parent interviews; picture-sociometric and writing exercise
main_finding: Identity references included birthplace, residence and parental accounts; newly arrived students expressed more certainty about Hong Kong identity than cross-boundary students, and Hong Kong schooling acted as an acculturative setting. The detailed sample shows that same-background and cross-background ties can coexist.
limitation: Mixed population includes nine daily cross-boundary students; one newly arrived child was not a transfer student and some were below Primary 4; tiny qualitative sample; the assimilation vocabulary should not be treated as a fixed endpoint.

title: From purification of 'sins' to negotiation of boundaries: exploring assimilation of children of Mainland new arrivals in Hong Kong secondary school context
population: Secondary students who were children of Mainland new arrivals, mixing Mainland-born 1.5 generation and Hong Kong-born second generation
study_design: in-depth interviews
main_finding: Participants had room to negotiate rather than merely adopt boundaries. They used and modified meanings in cultural products, including electronic games and television programmes, to build and sustain peer relationships.
limitation: The sample combines Mainland-born 1.5 generation and Hong Kong-born second generation, which the abstract does not disaggregate; small thesis sample; no evidence about named social-media platforms.

author_year: Cheung, Hoi Yan; Hui, Sammy King Fai (2003)
title: Mainland immigrant and Hong Kong local students' psychological sense of school membership
population: Mainland immigrant and local Hong Kong pupils in five schools; immigrant status meant self-reported Hong Kong residence of seven years or less
study_design: cross-sectional questionnaire; Chinese PSSM scale development and group comparison
main_finding: The Chinese PSSM was reliable in this sample. Mainland immigrant pupils reported significantly higher school belonging and lower rejection than local pupils, countering an assumption that immigrant status necessarily predicts low belonging.
limitation: Residence up to seven years includes early-childhood arrivals; prior Mainland schooling and insertion grade are unknown; five-school cross-sectional self-report; group mean differences do not explain mechanisms.

author_year: Chan, Stephen; Yuen, Mantak; Lau, Patrick S. Y. (2003)
title: The effects of a group guidance programme on the self esteem of newly arrived children from the Chinese Mainland to Hong Kong
population: Newly arrived Mainland children in one Hong Kong primary school
study_design: small quasi-experimental group-guidance evaluation with questionnaire and follow-up interviews
main_finding: After ten 90-minute sessions, the intervention group showed improvement in peer-relationship self-esteem and described gains in social skills; the article supports the possibility that school-based support can affect relational adjustment.
limitation: Non-random small groups in one school; one-tailed tests; short follow-up; one grade falls below target boundary; prior Mainland schooling and insertion point not fully specified.

title: The Educational Progress of Mainland Chinese Immigrant Students in Hong Kong
population: Mainland immigrant and native Hong Kong students in a representative longitudinal cohort of junior secondary schools
study_design: secondary analysis of the Medium of Instruction Longitudinal Survey cohort
main_finding: Mainland students began Form 1 above local peers in subjects other than English and gained more in most subjects; they narrowed but did not close the English gap. Low socioeconomic background and low-achieving schools did not explain the pattern, while school type and age moderated it.
limitation: Accessible abstract does not state sample size or the operational immigrant definition, arrival grade and prior schooling; cohort began in 1999–2000; longitudinal achievement does not capture lived adaptation.

author_year: Wu, Qiaobing; Ou, Ying; Jordan, Lucy P. (2021)
title: Contribution of family and school factors to the health and wellbeing of cross-border, new immigrant and local students in Hong Kong
population: New immigrant, daily cross-border and local students; new immigrants were Mainland-born and resident in Hong Kong for under seven years
study_design: cross-sectional school survey and regression analyses
main_finding: Results showed nuanced group differences: new immigrant students reported poorer wellbeing overall; parent-child interaction related differently to outcomes across groups, father relationship was especially salient for new immigrants, and teacher and peer relationships were associated with outcomes in all three groups.
limitation: Cross-sectional associations are not causal; schools were sampled in districts with higher immigrant shares; residence-under-seven-years does not establish arrival grade or substantial prior Mainland schooling; cross-border pupils are out of scope.

title: The adaptation of Chinese adolescents in two societies: A comparison of Chinese adolescents in Hong Kong and Australia
population: China-born adolescent migrants to Hong Kong and Australia, plus locally born comparison groups
study_design: cross-sectional questionnaire group comparison
sample_size: 779 total: 111 China-born migrants in Hong Kong; 55 Chinese migrants in Australia; 456 Hong Kong-born; 157 Anglo-Australian
main_finding: China-born migrants in Hong Kong showed relatively better sociocultural but poorer psychological adaptation than Chinese migrants in Australia; both migrant groups compared favourably with their non-migrant peers on some measures, illustrating that adaptation domains can diverge.
limitation: Arrival grade, years in Hong Kong and prior school history are unavailable in the accessible abstract; cross-national measures and selection differ; cross-sectional group differences are not migration effects.

title: Differential impacts of stressful life events and social support on the mental health of mainland Chinese immigrant and local youth in Hong Kong: A resilience perspective
population: Mainland Chinese immigrant and local youth
study_design: structured individual questionnaire/interview and group comparison
main_finding: Immigrant youth had similar stress exposure and, on average, better mental health than local youth in this sample. School change and parent conflict were additional risks, while peer support, endurance and social competence were protective correlates for immigrant youth.
limitation: Includes participants beyond school age; arrival grade, prior schooling and current enrolment are unclear; cross-sectional self-report; likely overlaps with earlier reports from the same 106-immigrant/104-local project, so outputs should not be counted as independent samples.

title: Envisioned Belonging: Cultural Differences and Ethnicities in Hong Kong Schooling
population: Mainland Chinese and South Asian immigrant teenagers in four Hong Kong secondary schools, with attention to teachers' constructions
study_design: multi-school ethnographic fieldwork
main_finding: Teachers identified cultural discrepancies for both Mainland and South Asian students but differed in assumptions about students' malleability and future belonging. The article develops 'envisioned belonging' and cautions against deficit explanations that locate adaptation solely in students.
limitation: Article combines immigrant groups; subgroup sample and insertion histories are not tabulated; teacher discourse and ethnographic interpretation do not establish prevalence.

author_year: Zhu, Jinxin; Kennedy, Kerry J.; Mok, Magdalena Mo Ching; Halse, Christine Margaret (2019)
title: Chinese immigrant students in Hong Kong: Exploring performance and influences on their civic learning
population: Hong Kong eighth graders classified in ICCS 2016, including Mainland Chinese immigrant-grant students
study_design: secondary analysis of ICCS 2016; two-level path analysis
main_finding: Mainland immigrant-grant students had higher civic knowledge at student level. Open classroom climate and conventional-citizenship importance were small positive mediators; family socioeconomic status via civic learning was a small negative mediator, while considerable variance occurred at school level.
limitation: Accessible abstract does not give immigrant subgroup size or establish actual residence migration, arrival grade or prior schooling; secondary cross-sectional data cannot identify adaptation trajectories; mediation language is associational.

author_year: Census and Statistics Department, Hong Kong SAR (2023)
title: 2021 Population Census Thematic Report: Persons from the Mainland Having Resided in Hong Kong for Less Than 7 Years
population: Mainland-born Chinese nationals with domicile in Hong Kong who had resided there for less than seven years
study_design: population census descriptive statistics
sample_size: 134845 persons in the defined population in 2021
main_finding: The 2021 Census counted 134,845 persons from the Mainland resident in Hong Kong for under seven years; 17.7% were under age 15. Reported school-attendance rates were 100% at ages 6–11 and 97.9% at ages 12–17.
limitation: The census category cannot identify prior Mainland schooling, insertion grade, local versus international school, or the target transfer subgroup; attendance is not adaptation; figures describe 2021, not the 2026 stock.

title: Education and Support Services for Newly-arrived Children
population: Newly arrived children, including Mainland children entering Hong Kong schools
study_design: policy and service documentation
main_finding: The Bureau documents placement assistance, a full-time six-month Initiation Programme before mainstream entry, a 60-hour Induction Programme run in parallel with schooling, and school-based support arrangements. These pages establish the support architecture, not uptake or effectiveness.
limitation: Live administrative pages show no clear publication date; no participant sample, outcome evaluation, utilisation rate or target-subgroup breakdown; programme availability must not be equated with adequate support.

author_year: Peter F. Titzmann; Richard M. Lee (2018)
title: Adaptation of Young Immigrants: A Developmental Perspective on Acculturation Research
population: young immigrants
study_design: developmental and acculturation literature review
main_finding: Acculturation in young people is dynamic and intertwined with normative development; treating adaptation as a static endpoint understates age, timing, transitions, and changing developmental tasks.
limitation: Conceptual review rather than a systematic review; no Hong Kong or school-transfer sample; offers no direct estimate for the target population.

author_year: Seth J. Schwartz; Jennifer B. Unger; Byron L. Zamboanga; José Szapocznik (2010)
title: Rethinking the Concept of Acculturation: Implications for Theory and Research
population: international migrants and descendants
study_design: integrative conceptual review
main_finding: Heritage and receiving-culture practices, values, and identifications are separable dimensions that may change at different rates; context of reception constrains apparent choices, and proxy measures such as language or years of residence are inadequate substitutes for acculturation.
limitation: Broad review with substantial United States health-research emphasis; national categories are not cultures; not specific to minors, schools, Hong Kong, or cross-system transfer.

title: Revisiting the Integration Hypothesis: Correlational and Longitudinal Meta-Analyses Demonstrate the Limited Role of Acculturation for Cross-Cultural Adaptation
population: migrants and ethnic-minority participants in prior studies
study_design: reanalysis and longitudinal meta-analysis
sample_size: correlational meta-analysis: k=83, N=23197; longitudinal meta-analysis: k=19, N=6791
main_finding: Cross-sectional associations were weaker than commonly implied and longitudinal associations were very small; the authors conclude that evidence for acculturation orientations as drivers of later adaptation is limited.
limitation: Only 19 longitudinal studies; heterogeneous constructs, timings, and populations; mixed migrant generations; subsequent methodological critique and reanalysis dispute the strength of this conclusion.

author_year: Dmitry Grigoryev; John W. Berry; Maria Stogianni; Angela-MinhTu D. Nguyen; Michael Bender; Verónica Benet-Martínez (2023)
title: The integration hypothesis: A critical evaluation informed by multilevel meta-analyses of three multinational datasets
population: migrant and ethnocultural groups represented in three existing multinational datasets
study_design: three-level meta-analytic reanalysis
sample_size: three multinational datasets; exact combined N not entered because it was not consistently stated on the accessible page
main_finding: Across the reanalysed datasets, integration was positively associated with adaptation, especially positive indicators; contextual moderators and discrimination explained some heterogeneity. The authors emphasize that the framework is structural and correlational rather than a causal law.
limitation: Reuses observational datasets; operationalization and analytic choices are contested; exact sampling differs across datasets; not specific to Hong Kong, school transfer, or adolescents.

author_year: Kelly A. Allen; Margaret L. Kern; Dianne Vella-Brodrick; John Hattie; Lea Waters (2018)
title: What Schools Need to Know About Fostering School Belonging: a Meta-analysis
population: school students in 51 studies
study_design: systematic review and meta-analysis
main_finding: Teacher support and positive personal characteristics were among the strongest correlates of school belonging; associations varied across study contexts, including geography.
limitation: Most included evidence was correlational; belonging definitions and instruments were heterogeneous; not focused on migrants, transfer students, or Hong Kong.

author_year: Amina Abubakar; Fons J. R. van de Vijver; Itziar Alonso-Arbiol; Angela O. Suryani; Weny Savitry Pandia; Penny Handani; Josephine Arasa; Lubna Mazrui; Margaret Murugumi (2016)
title: Assessing Sense of School Belonging Across Cultural Contexts Using the PSSM: Measurement and Functional Invariance
population: students in four cultural contexts
study_design: confirmatory factor analysis and measurement-invariance testing
main_finding: Item-level one-factor and bifactor models did not fit adequately, whereas a target-parceled one-factor solution showed cross-context invariance and high reliability; the relation with life satisfaction was also invariant.
limitation: Participants were not migrants and Hong Kong was not included; broad age range; parceling can conceal item-level noninvariance; cross-sectional validation.

author_year: Xiaoxue Kuang; Magdalena Mo Ching Mok; Ming Ming Chiu; Jinxin Zhu (2019)
title: Sense of school belonging: Psychometric properties and differences across gender, grades, and East Asian societies
population: Grade 4 and Grade 8 students
study_design: secondary survey analysis using Rasch modelling, differential item functioning, and multigroup multilevel models
main_finding: After removal of an unrelated item, the measure showed acceptable psychometric properties, but some items displayed society- and grade-related differential functioning; girls generally reported higher belonging, and belonging was lower in Grade 8 than Grade 4 in the reported comparisons.
limitation: Not a migrant or transfer-student study; secondary cross-sectional survey; a short scale may omit mechanisms; differential item functioning complicates direct mean comparisons.

title: The Making and Unmaking of Ethnic Boundaries: A Multilevel Process Theory
population: ethnic groups and boundary processes in comparative cases
study_design: multilevel comparative theory building
main_finding: Ethnic boundaries are outcomes of classificatory struggles and negotiations rather than fixed cultural distances; institutional order, power distributions, and political networks shape available boundary-making strategies.
limitation: Macro-comparative theory; no adolescent, school, digital, Hong Kong, or transfer-student sample; requires careful micro-level operationalization for everyday peer interaction.

author_year: Jean S. Phinney; Gabriel Horenczyk; Karmela Liebkind; Paul Vedder (2001)
title: Ethnic Identity, Immigration, and Well-Being: An Interactional Perspective
population: immigrants and ethnocultural minorities
study_design: conceptual and empirical literature review
main_finding: The proposed interactional model treats identity and well-being as products of both migrant characteristics and the receiving context; strong ethnic and national identifications were often associated with better adaptation in the reviewed evidence.
limitation: Narrative review from an earlier literature; much evidence is correlational; country and group coverage is selective; later meta-analytic disagreement limits any universal dual-identity claim.

title: Cultural Brokering in Immigrant Families
population: immigrant children, adolescents, and emerging adults in family settings
study_design: focused conceptual review
main_finding: Cultural brokering is context-dependent and includes distinct interpersonal and socializing forms; reported consequences are mixed, highlighting developmental stage, relationship context, and youths' interpretations.
limitation: Family-centered review; cultural brokering is broader than but overlaps language brokering; no direct evidence about peer bridges, Hong Kong schools, or transfer students; not a meta-analysis.

title: Polymedia: Towards a new theory of digital media in interpersonal communication
population: members of transnational families
study_design: comparative ethnography and theory development
main_finding: Polymedia describes an integrated communicative environment in which each medium is understood relationally to the others; when access and cost constraints recede, medium choice acquires relational, emotional, and moral significance.
limitation: Developed mainly from transnational-family ethnography; sample details were not fully available on the accessed publisher page; assumes meaningful access to a repertoire; platform ecology predates current Mainland-Hong Kong governance and apps.

title: How to research cross-media practices? Investigating media repertoires and media ensembles
population: media users and social collectivities
study_design: theory and methods article
main_finding: The article distinguishes individual media repertoires from media ensembles shared within social domains and proposes triangulating diaries, interviews, group methods, and sorting tasks to connect the two levels.
limitation: Methodological article without a migrant-youth or Hong Kong sample; intensive designs create participant burden and reactivity; platform configurations change quickly.

title: Spinning the web of identity: the roles of the internet in the lives of immigrant adolescents
population: teenage immigrants from the former Soviet Union living in Israel
study_design: in-depth qualitative interviews
main_finding: Participants described the internet as a resource for personal growth, empowerment, relationships, and evolving identity while negotiating settlement-related disadvantage.
limitation: Single origin-receiving context; qualitative self-report; pre-smartphone and early social-media ecology; no longitudinal or causal design; not specifically a school-transfer study.

author_year: Fleur Prinsen; Mariëtte de Haan; Kevin M. Leander (2015)
title: Networked Identity: How Immigrant Youth Employ Online Identity Resources
population: Dutch-Moroccan students from two inner-city schools
study_design: semi-structured ego-network interviews with VennMaker and NodeXL plus qualitative content analysis
sample_size: 24 interviewed; 16 retained for final network-typology comparison
main_finding: Online and offline networks varied substantially: online ties sometimes extended identity resources, sometimes maintained family or ethnically homogeneous ties, and sometimes were less important than offline relationships. No single platform effect characterized all participants.
limitation: Small selected sample from two schools; mostly second generation; cross-sectional; low internet users were excluded and ambiguous cases were omitted from final typology; not a recent-arrival study.

title: Digital Passages: Migrant Youth 2.0: Diaspora, Gender and Youth Cultural Intersections
population: primarily Moroccan-Dutch youth recruited through secondary schools
study_design: mixed methods: school survey, in-depth interviews, participatory internet maps, and virtual ethnography
sample_size: survey N=1408; Moroccan-Dutch survey subgroup N=344; qualitative interviews N=43
main_finding: Digital practices both reproduced and transformed social boundaries; identity and belonging were intersectional and context-specific, and online and offline life could not be separated into a simple empowerment-versus-exclusion contrast.
limitation: Mostly second-generation youth in the Netherlands; data from 2009-2013 and now-dated platforms; school recruitment and subgroup analyses limit generalization; broad book-length design is not directly replicable by undergraduates.

author_year: Karmele Mendoza Pérez; Marta Morgade Salgado (2020)
title: Mobility and the mobile: A study of adolescent migrants and their use of the mobile phone
population: unaccompanied Moroccan migrant minors in a residential facility
study_design: 15-month ethnographic context plus participatory art workshop, maps, documentary, field notes, images, and interviews
sample_size: 5 focal migrant participants, with 2 local social-integration trainees in the workshop
main_finding: Mobile phones served as customizable private spaces, supported transnational memories and ties, and enabled local-global youth identity work, while institutional rules, connectivity, and access materially constrained practices.
limitation: Very small single-facility sample with distinctive unaccompanied-minor conditions; participatory researcher effects; not a school-peer sample; platform ecology and migration regime differ sharply from Hong Kong.

author_year: Carola Suárez-Orozco; Jean Rhodes; Michael Milburn (2009)
title: Unraveling the Immigrant Paradox: Academic Engagement and Disengagement Among Recently Arrived Immigrant Youth
population: recently arrived immigrant youth in the Longitudinal Immigrant Student Adaptation study
study_design: five-year longitudinal comparative study and structural-equation modelling
main_finding: The study identified differing trajectories of engagement and achievement after arrival and found that supportive relationships were statistically linked to engagement and outcomes in the longitudinal models.
limitation: Nonrandom urban United States sample; heterogeneous origins; attrition and self-report concerns; observational mediation does not establish causation; no digital-platform focus and no Hong Kong context.

title: 方言能力、学校融合与流动儿童心理健康发展
population: 中国教育追踪调查中的流动儿童
study_design: CEPS二手数据的横截面回归、机制与异质性分析
sample_size: 识别流动儿童1769人; 完整分析样本1279人
main_finding: 方言能力与心理健康呈正向统计关联，学校互动、学校认同和同伴接纳在模型中解释了部分关联；学校同伴构成与关联强度有关。作者将其解释为学校融合渠道，但设计不能确证因果。
limitation: 横截面自陈数据和中介模型不能识别因果; 学校认同与同伴接纳量表信度偏低; 缺失数据后样本减少; 中国内地户籍流动与内地迁港制度情境不同。

title: Conducting focus groups with children and young people: strategies for success
population: children and young people participating in focus-group research
study_design: methodological review and practical guidance
main_finding: Focus groups with minors require substantial preparation and skilled facilitation; design choices should support data quality and a positive, developmentally appropriate participant experience.
limitation: Healthcare-oriented methodological discussion; not an empirical comparison of techniques; predates current digital and hybrid research; group privacy, peer dominance, and identity-sensitive disclosure require additional safeguards.
